title: [AMF/MME] Incorrect context lifecycle after Accept retransmission exhaustion

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

body:
## Summary

When a UE does not send the expected Complete message and Accept retransmissions are exhausted, the AMF and MME both enter a generic exception state, but their cleanup paths differ:

| Component | Timeout behavior identified |
| --- | --- |
| AMF / T3550 | Releases PDU sessions and removes the AMF UE context without deleting the AMF's UDM SDM subscription. Repeated occurrences accumulate orphaned subscriptions. |
| MME / T3450 | Enters exception and stops all UE/bearer timers, but the timer dispatcher does not initiate session/context cleanup. An aborted Attach can retain resources without a cleanup timer. |

These paths need procedure-specific handling. In particular, LTE Attach timeout requires a different registration state from 5G initial-registration timeout.

## Steps to reproduce

### AMF: Registration Complete not received

1. Register an authenticated UE and establish a PDU session.
2. Send an integrity-protected mobility Registration Request that causes Registration Accept and an expected Registration Complete.
3. Keep the NG connection alive, but omit Registration Complete for the initial Accept and every retransmission.
4. Wait for T3550 exhaustion, then complete the NGAP UE Context Release procedure initiated by the AMF.
5. Inspect the UDM's SDM subscriptions. Repeat registration and timeout for the same subscriber.

### MME: Attach Complete not received — proposed reproduction

1. Start an authenticated LTE Attach and proceed through authentication, security mode control, session creation, and delivery of Attach Accept.
2. Keep the S1 connection alive, but omit Attach Complete for the initial Accept and every retransmission.
3. Wait for T3450 exhaustion. Inspect the EMM state, UE/bearer timers, and whether any S11 Delete Session Request or S1AP UE Context Release Command is sent.
4. Keep the UE silent and check whether its UE, S1, and session contexts remain allocated.
5. Separately, request normal S1 release from the eNB after the timeout and check whether later reachability/implicit-detach cleanup is scheduled.

Both timers default to 6 seconds with four retransmissions: one initial Accept plus four retransmissions, followed by the fifth expiry at approximately 30 seconds. A radio release or transport failure before exhaustion can take a different path.

## Observed behavior / source analysis

### AMF

1. [T3550 exhaustion](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/amf/gmm-sm.c#L3654-L3660) transitions to `gmm_state_exception`.
2. [Exception entry](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/amf/gmm-sm.c#L3781-L3799) releases all SM contexts. The [release-response exception path](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/amf/nsmf-handler.c#L1571-L1583) ultimately sends `NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_UE_CONTEXT_REMOVE`.
3. [NGAP release completion](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/amf/ngap-handler.c#L2136-L2146) removes the UE. [`amf_ue_remove()`](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/amf/context.c#L1830-L1937) frees local handles without sending SDM unsubscribe, UECM deregistration update, or PCF AM-policy deletion.

The SMF's subscription was deleted during session release; the AMF's was not. PCF cleanup omission was identified in source rather than measured.

### MME

1. [T3450 exhaustion](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/mme/emm-sm.c#L1776-L1783) transitions from `emm_state_initial_context_setup` to `emm_state_exception`.
2. [Exception entry](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/mme/emm-sm.c#L1880-L1884) only clears the service indicator and all UE/bearer timers.
3. The [EMM message dispatcher](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/mme/mme-sm.c#L435-L438) calls `mme_send_delete_session_or_mme_ue_context_release()` when the FSM remains in exception. The [timer dispatcher](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/mme/mme-sm.c#L442-L451) has no equivalent check.
4. A subsequent normal S1 release does not restore the cleanup lifecycle: [release completion](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/2449ff80f3682ec95fdd92d6d27c084b29b50f67/src/mme/s1ap-handler.c#L2295-L2309) starts the mobile-reachable timer only in `emm_state_registered`.

Resources can therefore remain until another NAS message or an independent cleanup path intervenes. The duration and scale still need runtime verification.
